class.name: ResourceImporterVirtualTexture
class.brief_description: Imports an image as a [VirtualTexture2D], streamed a page at a time.
class.description: This importer turns an image into a [VirtualTexture2D]: a texture cut into pages, which are only loaded into video memory once the camera samples them. Use it for textures too large to keep in video memory whole, such as a terrain's or a large building's unique texture. Images are not imported this way on their own. Right-click one or more images in the FileSystem dock and choose [b]Convert to Virtual Texture[/b]: they are reimported with this importer, keeping their normal map setting, and every reference to them is kept. [b]Convert to Regular Texture[/b] reimports them as ordinary textures again. Both sides of the texture are resized to the closest power of two, from [constant RenderingServer.VIRTUAL_TEXTURE_PAGE_SIZE] to 131072 texels (see [member process/size_limit]).

members.member: The quality of the pages' WebP compression, when [member compress/mode] is Lossy. Higher values look better and take more room on disk.
How pages are compressed on disk; see [enum VirtualTexture2D.PageFormat]. In video memory they are always uncompressed, but only a fixed number of them is resident at once.
If [code]true[/code], the texture is a normal map: its mipmaps are renormalized as they are made, rather than only averaged. It is set when converting a texture that was imported as a normal map.

If [code]true[/code], pages along the texture's edges are bordered with texels from its opposite edge, so that it repeats seamlessly. Turn this off for a texture that is never repeated, such as one covering a whole terrain, so that its edges are not blended with each other.
If greater than [code]0[/code], the texture is downscaled so that neither side is larger than this, in texels, rounded down to a power of two.
